summary: Our idea was to create a program where the user selects a date, time, and location on the lunar surface and receives a visualization of the Moon's illumination at that site, along with information on the feasibility of communication with Earth, whose position is also visible in the simulation. The program also returns data such as Sun Angle on Surface, Sun Elevation Horizon, and Solar Efficiency Factor. Importantly, our solution allows selecting any point on the lunar surface and moving the marker using the WASD keys, which can be useful when searching for new landing sites. The presented version of the program allows searching for dates ranging from November 14, 2026, to November 14, 2028.
details: Using data from JPL Horizons Systems, we created an application in Unity that simulates the motion and relative positions of the Moon, Earth, and Sun. We used real data from LOLA to build a 3D model of the Moon using Python, so the model viewed by the user reflects the actual shadowing of a given area, allowing us to determine access to solar energy. The program returns data such as Sun Angle on Surface, Sun Elevation Horizon, and Solar Efficiency Factor. Our solution allows selecting any point on the lunar surface and moving the marker using the WASD keys, which can be useful when searching for new landing sites. The presented version of the program allows searching for dates ranging from November 14, 2026, to November 14, 2028, because we use ephemerides from files generated by the JPL Horizons tool. In the next version of the program, the controls should be improved, and data should be fetched directly from the JPL Horizons System using its API.
